name: Ehrwald
kurzbeschreibung: Starting point for the Zugspitze with Germany’s highest mountain right on your doorstep and the Zugspitzarena at your fingertips.
title: Ehrwald
metaDescription: Ehrwald in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena: At the foot of Mount Zugspitze, Tiroler Zugspitzbahn cable car, Ehrwalder Alm, Seebensee, Drachensee and UNESCO solstice fires.
text:
Overview

Ehrwald is situated at an elevation of 994 meters in the district of Reutte, serving as the largest municipality in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena. Home to approximately 2,600 residents, this vibrant alpine resort spreads across a wide, sunlit valley basin at the base of the Wetterstein mountain range. Rising directly above the village is the sheer west face of Mount Zugspitze (2,962 m), Germany's highest peak, while the jagged crests of the Mieminger chain with the Ehrwalder Sonnenspitze border the valley to the south. Renowned internationally, Ehrwald blends top-tier winter and summer sports with pristine mountain lakes such as Seebensee and Drachensee alongside rich cultural heritage.

History

Settlement in the Ehrwald basin dates back to the thirteenth century, with the earliest documented mention recorded in 1274 as Erwalden. Etymologically, the name stems from Old High German, signifying the beginning of the forest. Historically, local livelihoods depended on farming, timber harvesting, barrel stave production for the royal salt mines in Hall in Tirol, and trade over the Fern Pass. Lead and zinc mining flourished for a time in the nearby Igelskar cirque. The parish church of the Visitation was erected between 1640 and 1648, gaining its distinctive baroque onion-domed tower in 1769. In 1926, the inauguration of the Tiroler Zugspitzbahn represented a monumental alpine engineering milestone as Tyrol's very first passenger cable car. An extraordinary tradition is the Ehrwald Solstice Fires, where mountaineers illuminate mountain crags with flaming religious and heraldic motifs, officially inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2010.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, Ehrwald is reached completely toll- and vignette-free from Munich via Garmisch-Partenkirchen along roads B23 and B187 in approximately 75 minutes. From Kempten or Füssen, scenic toll-free driving follows route B179 via Reutte and Lermoos. From Innsbruck, drivers take motorway A12 across the Mieminger Plateau and over the Fern Pass. Rail travelers benefit from direct service on the Außerfernbahn line: Ehrwald Zugspitzbahn railway station is served hourly by direct trains connecting Garmisch-Partenkirchen (with ICE links to Munich) and Kempten. Locally, the Zugspitz Arena bus system provides frequent transfers between the station, village center, and all cableway base stations, free of charge for guest card holders.

Tips

Ascending to 2,962 meters aboard the panoramic Tiroler Zugspitzbahn from Ehrwald-Obermoos delivers an awe-inspiring four-country alpine vista and access to the interactive Fascination Zugspitze museum. Hikers and mountain bikers flock to the Ehrwalder Alm plateau, continuing towards the turquoise waters of Seebensee and the higher Drachensee lake below Coburger Hütte. In winter, the Ehrwalder Alm ski area boasts 27.5 kilometers of family-friendly slopes and floodlit night tobogganing, complemented by sunny runs at the Wettersteinbahnen. Trail runners celebrate Ehrwald as a focal hub of the world-famous Zugspitz Ultratrail event. A peaceful nature stroll winds through Gaisbach gorge to the rushing Ehrwald Waterfall.
